critical_evidence.evidence: Carfax shows oil and filter changes at regular intervals from 2020 to 08/01/2026. The brake fluid was flushed on 11/22/2025, within the last year. All work was done at Preston Mazda.

The NICB entry dates manufacture to 08/13/2019. That is an ND2 car built well after the revised 6MT internals, so the early-ND1 gearbox weak point does not apply. Carfax shows no reported transmission repair entries. A warm-shift check at PPI is still sensible.
The RF has targa seals and drains rather than soft-top drains. There are no photos with the carpet lifted or of the drain and seal areas. The interior photo shows clean upholstery only.

Carfax reports 'No open recalls reported.' NHTSA lists 21V875 (fuel pump) and 24V695 (airbag control module software) as campaigns that may cover this car. No service entry shows that the work was performed, so confirm with a Mazda VIN lookup.
Carfax shows a dated battery replacement on 11/22/2025, an oil service on 08/01/2026 and tires mounted on 10/25/2023. Tire DOT date-code photos have been requested but not yet received.

documentation.rationale: Identity and terms are strong: VIN-decoded trim, an itemised OTD worksheet ($26,087.97 excluding CA tax and shipping), and a guaranteed clean title. Maintenance evidence is strong: an 18-entry Carfax with time-based oil service, a 2025 brake fluid flush and a 2025 battery. What is missing is photos or inspection of the at-risk areas (underbody, targa seals and footwells, tire codes), and the records are summary lines rather than invoices.

condition.rationale: Photos show straight panels, clean Auburn leather, factory wheels and no visible damage. The service cadence is consistent, and no fault is stated. The dealer inspection report, underbody, roof function, tire dates and scan data are not yet seen. The 'nothing wrong' comment is a second-hand seller claim.

price_value.rationale: The $24,998 list plus a $989 fee sits above the fair value band of $21,723–$23,591 (mid $22,804). The list price alone is about 10% over mid. The rarer GT-S and colour combination explains part of the premium but not all of it, and there are no known-work deductions.

mission_fit.rationale: Manual RF, ND2 engine, a low-maintenance platform, and an asking price under the $27,000 maximum. It is a usable year-round daily if the roof seals check out. It is available now, with a dealer ready to transact.

logistics.rationale: Alexandria, VA is about 2,355 miles away. The dealer is responsive and documentation is moving. A mobile PPI on the lot is plausible but not yet arranged, and deposit refundability is unstated. A CA smog check and out-of-state registration are needed.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: This is Jason's top preference on every axis: Machine Gray, Auburn Nappa, Grand Touring with GT-S (Bilstein, LSD, brace), the 181 hp ND2 engine, RF and manual. It also has one owner and appears stock.

ppi_focus: Underbody corrosion check (salt-region car): subframes, brake and fuel lines, suspension fasteners, exhaust hangers
RF roof: cycle 3+ times, listen for rattles or creaks, check targa seals and drains, and look for water tracks or damp carpet and seat-rail corrosion
Gearbox warm-shift test across all gears, plus clutch slip check in 4th-6th under load and engagement point
LSD function, and rear diff pinion and output seal seepage
Water pump weep hole and coolant crust, plus valve cover and front crank seal seepage
Bilstein damper leaks, and end-link or bushing noises over bumps
Paint-meter readings on the aluminum hood and fenders, rock-chip and respray check, wheel curb rash
Tire DOT dates and wear pattern, including any alignment wear
Full OBD scan, and recall status confirmed by VIN at a Mazda dealer
Infotainment touchscreen for ghost touch or delamination, and CMU stability
what_would_change_verdict: A clean mobile PPI with a dry, low-corrosion underbody and a properly cycling, leak-free roof would move it up
A price negotiated toward the $22,800 fair-value mid would materially improve value
Significant underbody rust, roof faults or water ingress would move it down
An unexplained intermediary owner behind the 10/13/2026 Delaware title, or a non-refundable deposit with no PPI allowed, would move it down
evidence.mission_note: This is a genuine enthusiast fit, not merely a pragmatic bridge: a manual ND2 RF in Jason's preferred colours and GT-S spec, low-maintenance, and easy to resell within 6-24 months. Accelerated-bridge mode still calls for a PPI and price discipline before money moves.
evidence.rationale: The Carfax and VIN decode establish a 2019 RF Grand Touring with 34,926 miles, one estimated owner since 2019, a guaranteed clean title, and no reported accident, damage or total loss. Records are dealer-only and consistent, covering regular oil service through 08/01/2026. Time-based items appear too: a brake fluid flush and battery replacement on 11/22/2025, and tires mounted in 10/2023. The photos confirm Machine Gray paint, Auburn Nappa leather, a manual shifter, factory wheels and no visible body damage. Nothing mechanically wrong is observed. Observed issues are a list price about 10% above the $22,804 fair-value mid, a Delaware title issued 16 days before listing, and a worksheet carrying someone else's address. Still open: underbody condition after seven Eastern Shore winters, roof and targa seal function, tire date codes, recall completion, the dealer's inspection report, and whether a PPI can happen before a deposit is placed.
evidence.next_action: Ask Amin in writing to confirm the $1,000 deposit is refundable on a failed inspection and to allow a mobile PPI on the lot. Then book an independent inspector in Alexandria, briefed on the underbody, roof, targa seals, tires and recall checks above.
